messages:
carla: quick FYI — customer onprem install (priv-deploy v2024.04) reported that a telemetry sidecar made calls to the cloud IMDS and retrieved short-lived creds. secops-bot raised an alert.
secops-bot: [ALERT] 2024-05-02T14:05:10Z sidecar-telemetry: unexpected call to 169.254.169.254 from kube-system/telemetry-sidecar-0
noah: ugh. how is a pod without hostNetwork or hostPID hitting IMDS? any kube-proxy or host-route magic?
li: root cause looks like a host-level NAT rule that was added to support hostGateway-based hostPort mapping: iptables MASQUERADE accidentally allowed pod->host SNAT to access host network interfaces; combined with a host proxy (socat) that forwards IMDS to host IP, pods could reach IMDS. repro steps on my laptop: run pod -> curl http://10.0.0.1:80 (host IP) -> forwarded to 169.254.169.254 -> token returned.
tess: this is slightly different from eBPF redirect issues we've seen. mitigation categories: 1) hard deny host-level forwarding to IMDS (iptables on host), 2) change CNI config to block hostGateway->host forwarding for pod subnets, 3) tighten net-agent capabilities (drop NET_RAW/CAP_NET_ADMIN), 4) change KMS client to not accept IMDS-sourced creds in private deploy.
carla: customer impact: if IMDS creds were retrieved, an attacker in a container could call KMS decrypt endpoints (depending on role). For private deployments we usually configure customer KMS over internal endpoints and require mTLS. We need to confirm whether the retrieved token was usable against our KMS proxy.
li: checking logs: telemetry-sidecar made a GET to /latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/role-name around 2024-05-02T13:58Z. No direct KMS API calls in the logs but we can't be sure.
noah: urgent triage steps I propose: 1) isolate node (cordon + drain) 2) collect /var/log/net-agent/* and host iptables-save 3) snapshot container filesystem 4) rotate any envelope keys that might map to that timeframe. Mark INF-4950.
tess: agree. For medium-term: enforce an OPA policy so private clusters reject addons that request hostGateway/hostPort or explicitly enable host networking for sidecars. Here's a minimal Rego rule to block hostNetwork or hostPort in pod spec for private deployments:
```
package redwood.admission

deny[msg] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Pod"
  (input.request.object.spec.hostNetwork == true)
  msg = "hostNetwork not allowed in private deployments"
}

deny[msg2] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Pod"
  some i
  container := input.request.object.spec.containers[i]
  container.ports[_].hostPort
  msg2 = "hostPort is disallowed in private clusters"
}
```
li: good. Also we should add a mutation/admission check that rewrites or strips annotations that allow the telemetry agent to create host-facing iptables rules.
carla: audit logging: we must ensure any IMDS/metadata access attempts are logged and forwarded. For private installs we recommended customers enable net-agent audit and forward to their SIEM. Sample rsyslog fragment I suggest:
```
# /etc/rsyslog.d/60-metadata-audit.conf
input(type="imfile" File="/var/log/net-agent/metadata-access.log" Tag="net-meta" Severity="warning")
action(type="omfwd" Target="logs.redwood.internal" Port="6514" Protocol="tcp" StreamDriver="gtls" StreamDriverMode="1")
```
noah: KMS note: do not accept ephemeral credentials from IMDS in private deployments. Our recommended flow for private is envelope keys provisioned via customer-admin action: HSM unwrap only over mutual-TLS endpoint, no reliance on metadata service. Priya (not on thread) already documented this but we need enforcement: a config flag like "kms.allow_imds=false" defaulted in private.
tess: infra needs a quick host-level iptables snippet we can push in user-data for hotfix. li, can you paste?
li: host iptables hotfix:
```
# drop IMDS access from pod CIDR on host
iptables -I FORWARD -s 10.244.0.0/16 -d 169.254.169.254 -j DROP
iptables -I PREROUTING -t nat -s 10.244.0.0/16 -d 169.254.169.254 -j REDIRECT --to-ports 65500
```
(we'll use DROP line; REDIRECT is for extra inspection in canary)
carla: important: ensure kube-proxy doesn't reinsert masquerade rules that undo this. Use persistent rules via nftables or host agent.
secops-bot: INF-4950 created: sidecar-imds-leak, severity=high, owners=noah, li, tess
noah: deployment plan: 1) push DROP rule to canary node pool (2 nodes) 2) enable net-agent audit forwarding, 3) run targeted key rotation if we find evidence of decrypt calls, 4) push OPA gate to reject hostNetwork/hostPort in private clusters. Rolling canary first.
li: I'll prepare a reconciliation job to scan host iptables/nft for any exceptions and report. Also will add a healthcheck that fails if IMDS reachable from pod network.
tess: docs: I'll add a section to Private Deploy security checklist: IMDS-hardening, KMS-mTLS-only, SA-permissions-minimum (no cluster-admin, restrict mountable secrets), OPA gates.
carla: action items (quick):
- li: push host iptables canary + healthcheck (ETA 90m)
- noah: start INF-4950 triage channel + runbook edits (ETA 45m)
- tess: OPA gate PR to repo (ETA EOD)
- carla: update private-deploy KMS config schema to default kms.allow_imds=false (ETA EOD)
Keep posting findings here. If we detect IMDS token use against KMS, escalate immediate envelope-key rotation. :lock:
